title: Audited probe-fork pipeline and tenant billing containment for nonblocking replicas
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: add an audited probe-forking path that sends lightweight copies of production requests to nonblocking replica workers while guaranteeing tenant-level cost containment, storage/cache isolation, and an auditable trail for experiments. This is aimed at enabling low-risk canary + shadow experiments without unbounded expenditure or accidental state pollution. Scope focuses on the proxy-level fork, per-tenant sampling and credit enforcement, telemetry tagging, and safe rollback hooks. Not in scope: full billing product changes; this ticket provides export hooks and accounting markers for billing to consume.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Replica path is opt-in per-route and per-tenant via config flag. 2) Forked requests are sampled or throttled by deterministic tenant-hash + reservoir to achieve stable probabilistic coverage. 3) Each tenant has configurable credit cap for forked traffic; enforcement happens at edge proxy and rejects forks past cap. 4) Forked requests cannot write to production caches, K/V, or telemetry stores; responses stored only in isolated ephemeral tenants. 5) Dashboards visualize fork volume, replica error rate delta against prod, and cost burn by tenant. 6) Auto-rollback triggers registered (error% or latency regression) and can demote replica traffic within 60s. 7) End-to-end tests and a staged rollout doc exist in Confluence.
design_notes: Architecture: at the edge proxy we implement a 'probe-fork controller' that: a) computes a stable sampling key using tenant_id+route; b) consults a lightweight token-bucket per-tenant (local cache backed by central meter) to decide fork allowance; c) annotates forked requests with an immutable audit header (X-RW-Probe: <id>) and routes to a separate 'replica plane' Kafka topic for queuing to replica workers. Replica workers run in a different tenant namespace with no write-through to shared KV/caches. To avoid double-warming caches, probe replicas should mark responses with 'no-cache' and the runtime will skip cache insertion for these paths. Cost accounting: fork events emit structured metric tags (probe=true, tenant=<id>, route=<>) to a cost-aggregation pipeline; enforcement can zero-charge or bill depending on tenant contract. Autosafety: controller exposes rollback hooks to console: on threshold breach, controller reduces sample rate to zero and flips a runtime flag that drops forks at proxy until manually cleared or until a configured cooldown expires.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: lab spike and synthetic load tests (staging) - feature flag off; Phase 2: enable for internal tenants only and run 24h smoke tests with credit caps - sample rate <= 1%; Phase 3: gated opt-in for customer tenants with sign-off from SRE and product - initial cap $10/day; Phase 4: gradual ramp for selected customers, monitor metrics for 72h; Phase 5: general availability and docs. Release gating: must have automated rollback working and budget enforcement in place.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for sampling logic and token-bucket enforcement. - Integration test that asserts forked requests do not write to KV or LRU caches. - Chaos test: induce replica worker latency/errors and verify auto-rollback triggers within SLAs. - Load test: ensure edge proxy fork-code adds <5% CPU overhead at target QPS. - End-to-end regression: compare production vs replica output diffs and ensure no increase in downstream error surface. Test artifacts: staging harness at https://ci.redwood.ai/jenkins/job/probe-fork/ and load report at https://perf.redwood.ai/reports/probe-fork-20250228.
metrics: Primary: forked requests/sec (per-tenant), fork success rate, replica error delta (replica_err_rate - prod_err_rate), cost burn by tenant (USD/day), sample rate effective (observed). Safety: rollback activation count, mean time to rollback (s). Performance: proxy p95 latency delta after enabling fork. All metrics are visible on Grafana board https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abC123/probe-fork-observability.
risks: 1) Undetected writes from replicas polluting caches or external systems; mitigated by strict runtime guards and integration tests. 2) Cost spikes if enforcement misconfigures; mitigated by conservative default caps and kill-switch. 3) Increased proxy overhead causing latency regression; mitigated by lightweight sampling and experimental throttles. 4) Audit trail gaps; mitigated via immutable headers and event emission to central audit topic.
